newsitem.title: INDIA: Tata Electric debt issue rated 'Baa3' by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Tata Electric debt issue rated 'Baa3' by Moody's.

text.p: India's Tata Electric Companies said on Friday that its proposed foreign currency bond issues under its Medium Term Notes programme for $300 million had been assigned a 'Baa3' rating by Moody's Investor Services.
Tata Electric Companies (TEC) is constituted of the Tata Power Co. Ltd., the Andhra Valley Power Supply Co. Ltd., and the Tata Hydro-Electric Power Supply Co Ltd.

"TEC has been assigned a 'Baa3' rating constrained by the sovereign ceiling from Moody's Investor Services for its proposed issue of unsecured debt aggregating $300 million," the firm said in a statement.
It said rating agency Standard & Poor's had also assigned a 'BB+' long term foreign currency rating with a positive outlook to the proposed bond issue.
"Standard & Poor have also assigned its 'BB+' foreign currency issuer credit rating with a positive outlook to TEC," the statement added.

"TEC therefore joins a very select group of India corporates whose Moody's credit rating has been constrained by the 'Baa3' long-term foreign currency rating of India, and who have received a 'BB+' rating with a positive outlook from Standard & Poor's," the statement added.
TEC is India's largest private sector utility engaged in the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity to the financial capital of Bombay.
